answer: New agents enter only through a voucher: an established agent stakes collateral on the newcomer and loses it if the newcomer cheats, so vouching for a fake costs a real sponsor. A public lantern registry lists every voucher bond, making fake identities easy to count. Sybils hit a mesa: each extra identity needs a fresh sponsor willing to risk collateral, so a hundred fakes cost a hundred bonds. A graph scan then flags clusters of identities funded from a single vertex, and the network freezes their trades until each proves separate backing.
